summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary at the Royal Asiatic Society and was a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875-1914).

Julius Euting was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier, later serving as director at the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire and professor at the University of Strasbourg.
Julius Evola was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at ITI L. Da Vinci and Sapienza University of Rome, and held a post at the Ahnenerbe from 1943 to 1945.

Julius Grill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Urach, Heidelberg, Jena, and Tübingen—where he completed his Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth—he served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at the University of Tübingen (1888-1913).

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Leipzig under Martin Haug, Albrecht Weber, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts as Tagore professor of law at Calcutta (1882-1883) and professor at Würzburg (1877-1920).

Julius Jüthner was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the German University of Prague and later held academic posts at the University of Fribourg (~1898-1903) and the University of Innsbruck (~1903-1937).

Julius Klaproth was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg, founded the Société Asiatique and Asiatisches Magazin, and held a chair at the University of Bonn (~1818-1835).
Julius Laber was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi in 1908. He also studied at the universities of Berlin, Freiburg, and Leipzig.

Julius Leumann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Geneva, Zurich, Leipzig, and Strasbourg under teachers including Ernst Leumann and Heinrich Hübschmann. He served as a teacher and later Rector (1906-1928) at Kantonsschule Frauenfeld.

Julius Lipner is a scholar of Indology, religion, and philosophy. Educated at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur University, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis, he taught at Birmingham before becoming Professor of Hinduism at the University of Cambridge (1975-2013).

Julius Mohl was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian studies who studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Burnouf. He was a professor at Tübingen (1826-1834) and professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847-1876).

Julius Müller was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1831-1835), University of Marburg (~1835-1839), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839-1878).

Julius Pokorny was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and Rudolf Much. He was a professor of Celtology at Berlin (1920-1935) and held later posts at Bern, Zurich, and Munich.
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Göttingen, the University of Bonn (~1858-1862), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.

Julius Schwab was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich under Martin Haug and Ernst Kuhn. He later worked as a librarian at the Badische Landesbibliothek and the Freiburg University Library.

Julius Wellhausen was a scholar of religion, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald, and held academic posts at Göttingen, Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, and Marburg.

Julius von Negelein was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Greifswald, Berlin, Marburg, and Königsberg. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Königsberg (1899) and full professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1920).

Juliusz J. Ossowski was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger and Richard von Garbe.

Jun Fujii is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2002-2008). He later joined Komazawa University, serving as a lecturer (~2011-2014) and as a professor in 2025.

Jun Takashima is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He served as an associate professor at Aichi Prefectural University and as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2020).
